title: The update gate and the switch-off list work: a build below the minimum gets "Please update Pexi", and a typo in the setting locks nobody out
evidence: Local throwaway server (own script, port 4311-4313): no setting -> GET /api/app-status = {"minVersion":null,"featuresOff":[]}; SHIN_APP_MIN_VERSION=2026-11-25.1 + SHIN_APP_FEATURES_OFF=share,feed,bogus -> {"minVersion":"2026-11-25.1","featuresOff":["share","feed","bogus"]}; SHIN_APP_MIN_VERSION=banana -> minVersion null. The server never reads the app's build (a ?v= and header made no difference); the phone compares itself. Client versionBelow(): 2026-11-18.1 vs min 2026-11-25.1 = true, equal = false, .10 vs .9 = false (numeric, correct), unknown/undefined build = false (never blocks). Live (2 requests): relay.anjiawenda.com/api/app-status = 200, minVersion null, access-control-allow-origin echoes both capacitor://localhost and https://localhost, so the shipped app can read it. 44 unit tests (review-prompt + remote-status) pass. app/src/app-status.ts, app/public/js/remote-status.js.
dup_of: R13 (adds: tested end to end locally and live; register had it as partial)

title: Using the gate needs a Mac settings edit plus a server restart, and works only if each build's APP_VERSION is bumped by hand; the runbook steps for R13 and R14 do not name the settings
evidence: settings: SHIN_APP_MIN_VERSION and SHIN_APP_FEATURES_OFF are read from the server environment (settings/src/index.ts:347-352), changed by editing ~/shin/mac/config.env and restarting (docs/readiness/RUNBOOK.md:47). RUNBOOK R13/R14 steps (lines 120-129) still say "After fix-app: raise the minimum version" and never name the setting; it is only in needs-jamin.md:276-279. APP_VERSION is a hand-typed date string (app/public/js/version.js:19, now 2026-11-18.1) separate from the Xcode build number (project.pbxproj CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 10); no script or test compares them or the last uploaded build. If a fix ships with the same APP_VERSION as the bad build, setting the minimum blocks both or neither. Only a stand-in with Mac login can flip it (HANDOVER.md line 22).
fix: Add two lines to RUNBOOK R13/R14 (setting name, edit config.env, restart, check /api/app-status); add a release step or test that APP_VERSION is greater than the last uploaded build.
dup_of: R13, R14 (adds: the runbook steps are stale and nothing ties APP_VERSION to the uploaded build)

title: Phased release for updates is only written in two notes, and the checklist they point to does not exist
evidence: docs/readiness/RUNBOOK.md:218 and needs-jamin.md:34 say "manual release ... phased release for updates" and cite RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md; find found no such file in the repo (already gap 58). Pausing a phased release is named in RUNBOOK.md:129. Version 1.0 has no phased option (phased release applies to updates), so the first public build has the gate and switch-off list as its only brake.
fix: Write the checklist (manual release, phased for updates, bump APP_VERSION, buy Plus once).
dup_of: gap 58 (adds: v1.0 itself cannot be phased, so the gate is the only brake)

title: The app does ask for a rating, only after a good answer, through Apple's own prompt
evidence: app/public/js/review-prompt.js header and shouldAskForReview: asks when the answer used Pexi's own prices and scored great or good, no thumbs-down or correction, at least the 3rd such win on 2 local days, not the first session, last two scans not misses, 120 days since the last ask; fires 1 s after the answer sheet closes and only when the camera is idle (camera.js:3432-3446). No Pexi-drawn dialog, no incentive. Plugin @capacitor-community/in-app-review 8.0.0 is in native/package.json and Podfile.lock:7. 44 tests pass. A separate user-started "Rate Pexi" row exists on the You screen.

title: Rating prompts may be rare at first and cannot be seen before launch
evidence: The ask needs a third own-prices win; shoppers with thin price coverage in their area get broad estimates, which never count (review-prompt.js WIN_BASIS = own_prices). Apple shows nothing in TestFlight and rations the real prompt itself, so the only signal is the review_asked event (records that Pexi asked, not that anything showed). The native plugin is not installed in this PC's native/node_modules (no @capacitor-community folder), so the wiring was checked only through Podfile.lock, not a build. How often it fires in real use is assumed.
fix: After launch week, count review_asked events against active shoppers; if low, lower MIN_WINS to 2.

title: Crash reports reach Pexi's server and are logged, but nothing watches them: a bad build raising errors for everyone is seen only if someone searches the log
evidence: Local run: POST /api/client-error with a report that included a deviceId and URLs -> 200 {"ok":true}; the stderr line {"where":"client.js_error", "detail":{"build":"2026-11-18.1","source":"main.js","line":3,"stack":"at f (main.js:3:4)"}} kept the build, dropped the deviceId and the query string. It is a log line only (app/src/client-errors.ts, server.ts:4165-4181): no table, no counter in /api/health, no mention in scripts/deadman-probe.mjs or app/src/watch.ts (grep for client.js_error: only server.ts, client-errors.ts, its test and needs-jamin.md:305). A global cap of 30 logged reports a minute (ClientErrorBudget) means a crash wave across thousands of phones shows as 30 lines and one client.js_error_flood line a minute, which only a person reading the log would notice. The app sends at most 5 per session (crash-report.js MAX_REPORTS). Native crashes are not captured at all (App Store Connect only).
fix: Count client.js_error per build in the last hour into /api/health and let the existing dead-man or watch job email when it passes a number; plus a weekly look at Xcode Organizer crashes.
dup_of: R09, R14 (adds: no alert, the 30 a minute cap hides a wave, nothing in health)

title: A shopper has no way to write to support from inside the app except the paywall footer and "Delete my data"
evidence: grep mailto: in app/public/js finds only screens/you.js:132 (the delete-my-data email); the only other mention of the address is the paywall footer line paywall_seller (ui-strings.js:85, "Sold by Jamin Xu (Pexi). Contact: useshinapp@gmail.com"). No Contact, Help or Send feedback row on the You screen; "Rate Pexi" and "Report a wrong price" are the only others. A shopper whose Plus did not unlock or whose scan failed has the App Store page's support link or nothing. The support page (docs/store/index.html) names useshinapp@gmail.com but states no reply time; the same Gmail inbox is the only channel and auto-reply plus forwarding to both founders is still a to-do (needs-jamin.md:95).
fix: Add a "Contact us" row to You that opens a mailto with the build number and (with consent text) nothing else; state "we reply within 2 business days" on the support page and in the auto-reply.
fix_cost: 1 hour app change plus the Gmail auto-reply, $0
dup_of: R18 (adds: no in-app contact row, no stated reply time anywhere shoppers read)

title: Written procedures exist for refunds, data access and data deletion, each naming the person and a time
evidence: docs/privacy/data-requests.md: owner Jamin Xu; clock starts on receipt; law is 30 days (PIPEDA s.8(3), Quebec P-39.1 s.32), own target 7 days; two-question ownership check, export then delete script on the Mac, RevenueCat delete, request log in ~/shin-privacy (outside git), backups clear in 15 days. Refunds: docs/readiness/TEMPLATES.md "Refund request" (Apple issues it, reportaproblem.apple.com) and "Refund or purchase by a child" (reply the same day, never contest a parent's refund); the support page and paywall say the same. Corrections: reply within three business days (TEMPLATES.md:97). Read for the deadline, check and log sections; the script steps were not run.
dup_of: R18, R22, R53 (adds: confirmed they name owner and speed)

title: Every support, refund and privacy procedure has one person and one machine: Jamin, with data requests needing the Mac script
evidence: data-requests.md "For: Jamin Xu"; steps 4 to 5 run a script on the Mac then clear RevenueCat; HANDOVER.md lists Gmail, RevenueCat and the Mac as Jamin only, "Jamin fills in" for the stand-in on most rows. TEMPLATES says a person sends every reply. The 30-day clock keeps running while Jamin is in exams or at the new job. No Aurik step in the data-request page.
fix: Name a second person who can run the export or delete script and read the inbox, and write it in HANDOVER.md.
dup_of: R22, R42 (adds: data requests specifically depend on the Mac script)

title: Overpass or Open Food Facts being down or slow does not stop a scan
evidence: Local server with SHIN_OVERPASS=http://127.0.0.1:1 (dead): GET /api/stores?cell=43.26,-79.92 -> 200 {"stores":[]} in 11 ms. With Overpass hung (accepts, never answers): 200 {"stores":[]} after 10,019 ms (server ceiling, stores.ts:314 AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)); the app stops waiting after 1.5 s (shops.js nearbyWithin default 1500 ms) and shows the bundled chain list. Open Food Facts: 4 s timeout, a 429 starts a cool-off, a failure is not cached and returns off_failed so the scan carries on (open-food-facts.ts:39, 140-188);. Open Prices is only called by the importer (price/src/openprices.ts, 15 s), never in a shopper's request.

title: RevenueCat and Claude being down degrade instead of block
evidence: RevenueCat: server asks with a 3 s timeout (scan-quota.ts:58-59), a subscriber confirmed within 24 h stays Plus through an outage, kept on disk across a restart; plus-lookup tests (hang forever, restart) pass 23/23 with the OFF and offline tests. The phone shows "plans unavailable" strings (paywall_failed). Claude: timeouts, maxRetries 0 and a circuit breaker after repeated failures (identify/src/range-ask.ts:144-161, 390-419); a shopper who declined Claude already gets a broad estimate. Client side of the paywall failure and the Claude-down screen were read in code, not run on a phone.

title: The app has no deadline on calls to Pexi's own server, so a slow Mac leaves a spinner until the phone's own network limit
evidence: Test (own script, node, SHIN_API_BASE set before importing app/public/js/api.js): dead address -> price(), search(), identify() fail in 1 to 8 ms with TypeError (the app's no-connection path) and quota() returns null; a server that accepts and never answers -> price, search, quota and identify were all still pending after 15,000 ms. api.js edgeFetch (line 256) has no AbortSignal; only an HTML answer becomes the "Pexi is busy" sheet. The shopper can cancel with "Cancel and go back to the viewfinder" (ui-strings.js:474), and the WebView's own limit (about a minute) is assumed, not measured.
fix: Wrap edgeFetch in a 20 s abort that becomes the existing busy or no-connection error.

title: Overpass is sent a user-agent that still says "shin-beta (price scanner, six testers)"
evidence: app/src/stores.ts:316 headers user-agent: 'shin-beta (price scanner, six testers)'. Overpass asks apps to identify themselves; at launch the name is the old project name and the count is wrong, and there is no contact. The Open Food Facts agent was already fixed (R35), this one was missed.
fix: Change it to Pexi plus the support address (same text as OFF_USER_AGENT).

title: French: three different words for one action, and the legal pages disagree with the app about what the paywall sells
evidence: The tab is "Scanner"/"scans" (nav_scan_word; paywall_heading "100 scans de codes-barres par semaine"), but you_no_meter (ui-strings.js:1452) says "Aucune limite de numérisations", savings_recent (1437) "Numérisés récemment", and terms-fr.html and privacy-fr.html say "100 balayages de codes-barres par semaine", "ce que vous balayez ou saisissez" (balayer means sweep or swipe, not scan). The French flag is off today (flags.js:83 languages: false), so this bites only when French is switched on (R43).
fix: Pick "scan" (as the app uses) and replace numérisation, numérisés and balayage everywhere.

title: French: tu and vous are mixed, against the file's own rule of tutoiement throughout, and one string names a screen that does not exist
evidence: voice-fr.js header: "Tutoiement throughout". But agree_* (ui-strings.js:1053-1066) uses vous: "Vous pouvez changer ce choix à tout moment dans l'écran Vous.", "Cochez la case", "vous obtenez une estimation large"; vd_report_word (1121) is "Votre signalement"; the nav tab and screen are "Toi" (nav_you, you_title). So the consent screen sends the shopper to "l'écran Vous", which is called Toi. The hosted privacy and terms pages use vous throughout; the app around them uses tu.
fix: Rewrite agree_* and vd_report_word in tu; change "l’écran Vous" to "la page Toi" (as setup_lines_note already says); decide once whether the legal pages stay formal.

title: French: strings that read as machine translation or are plain wrong
evidence: All 718 keys exist in French (none missing; 18 identical to English are legitimate: Photos, Sources, Canada, Certain, brand names). Awkward or wrong, with line numbers in app/public/js/ui-strings.js: 1475 you_corrections_row "Corrections par cent nommés" (unintelligible); 1183 conf_thin "Mince · 2 marchands" (literal "Thin"; "Peu de données"); 982-983 "Prix du milieu" (median; "Prix médian"); 1473 you_kind_typed "Écrit" (typed; "Saisi"); 1445-1446 "pouces en haut / pouces en bas"; 1242 lic_fallback_credit "La liste complète ... est ce qui n'a pas pu être chargé" (garbled, and "chargée" agreement); 938 screen_error_body "Quelque chose dessus a cassé"; 1036 note_strongest "Pexi est le plus fort sur les produits emballés"; 1441 savings_unreadable "Je n'ai pas pu lire tes scans" (first person in a settings row); 1397 share_conf_high "Confiant" while the same level elsewhere is "Certain" (1088); 1477 you_week_two_none "personne n'a deux semaines"; "tablette" for shelf (onboarding, cam strings) against "rayon" (1099, 1142), and "marchand" for seller; onboarding writes the brand "PEXI" in capitals.
fix: Have one native reader fix this list in one pass.

title: French: 15 questions are written with no space before the question mark, and some colons likewise, against the file's own rule
evidence: In the French block (ui-strings.js 849-1507), 15 strings end "?" with no space (tm_heading "Est-ce l'un de ceux-ci?" 1045; agree_claude_q 1057; cam_verdict_right_q 1176; cam_what_is_it 1172; market_title 1247; correct_which_shop 1227; correct_pick_h 1231; vd_suspect 1122) against 2 that follow the rule ("Qu'as-tu fait ?" 918). voice-fr.js has "perdus: undefined" (about line 450) and similar with no space before the colon, although face_label's own comment says French needs one (ui-strings.js:1488-1493). A native reader sees it at once.
fix: One search-and-replace for " ?" and non-breaking space before ":" in the French tables.

title: French shoppers who open the paywall or the You screen's legal rows get the English terms and privacy pages; the update screen and support page are English only
evidence: app/public/js/plus-config.js:55-58 has legalUrl(kind, lang) that returns the -fr.html pages, and screens/agree.js:78-79 uses it, but screens/paywall.js:302-303 and 358-359 and screens/you.js:456,460 use the English LEGAL_URLS directly. The paywall is where the Quebec consumer contract is formed. The "Please update Pexi" screen text is a hard-coded English string (remote-status.js updateScreenHtml), not read from ui-strings. docs/store/index.html (support) exists only in English and both French legal pages link their "Soutien Pexi" link to it. No French store listing (gap 61). Only matters when French is switched on.
fix: Use legalUrl(kind, lang) in paywall.js and you.js; route the update screen text through t(); add a French support page.
dup_of: R43, gap 61 (adds: the paywall and You links, the update screen, the support page)
